labels.text: Product, route and clinical response must agree
Use the product-specific topical delivery method; never inject into the circulation.
Match the factor deficiency and inhibitor status to the exact therapy.
Assess clinical hemostasis with product-specific laboratory and safety monitoring.
Stabilize fibrin without losing route, renal, or thrombotic control
Match the indication and timing; eligible trauma or postpartum treatment need not wait for proof of fibrinolysis.
Keep tranexamic acid physically and visually separated from neuraxial drugs.
Renal elimination makes dose and toxicity surveillance patient specific.
Risk starts the therapy, and risk resolution stops it
Coagulopathy, shock, and chronic liver disease carry the clearest current signal.
Use a low-dose enteral or intravenous option when risk justifies exposure.
Discontinue when risk resolves and avoid an unnecessary discharge medicine.
